Your Character Builder character, ready for the table: take damage and heal, roll death saves, spend hit dice, tick off spell slots, rage, ki, and every other class resource, then take a short or long rest. The play sheet uses the characters saved by the Character Builder in this browser; hit points, slots, and the rest are saved with the character as you go, so they're still there after a reload, in an export, and in the Privacy page backup. Rolls go into the same history as the 🎲 dice button and the Dice Roller. A character in the party (👥 Add to Party) also shows its hit points, conditions, and concentration on the DM Toolbox's Party tab and in the Initiative tracker, live, when they're open in this same browser. Nothing is sent anywhere.

How to use a digital D&D character sheet at the table

Build the character once in the Character Builder, then open it here (the ▶️ Play button on its sheet) for the session. The builder does the math; the play sheet keeps track of what changes from turn to turn.

Hit points and dropping to 0

  • Type an amount, then Damage, Heal, or Temp HP. Damage takes temporary hit points first, and temporary hit points don't stack: the higher amount stays.
  • At 0 hit points the sheet shows your death saves. Roll them from the sheet: 10 or higher is a success, a natural 1 counts as two failures, and a natural 20 brings you back with 1 hit point. Three successes and you're stable; three failures and you're dead. Taking damage at 0 counts as a failure (tap a failure pip again for a critical hit, which counts as two). Damage that leaves as much over as your hit point maximum kills outright.
  • Concentrating on a spell? Taking damage shows the Constitution save you need (DC 10 or half the damage, whichever is higher), with a button to roll it.

Rests

  • Short Rest: spend hit dice one at a time (each heals one die plus your Constitution modifier), then finish the rest. Pact slots and short-rest features such as Action Surge, Channel Divinity, Ki, and Wild Shape come back.
  • Long Rest: hit points to full, temporary hit points gone, spell slots and every rest-based feature back, half your hit dice back (at least one), and one level of exhaustion off. Tap it twice to confirm.
  • Wizards and Circle of the Land druids recover some spell slots on a short rest: use Arcane Recovery or Natural Recovery, then tap the used slots you get back.

Rolling from the sheet

Click an ability for a check, its save button for a saving throw, a skill, Initiative, or an attack's Hit and Damage buttons. Advantage and Disadvantage stay on until you switch back to Normal. Crit doubles an attack's damage dice. Each roll is labeled with the character's name in the shared roll history.

Conditions and exhaustion

Tap a condition to mark it and see what it does. Exhaustion runs from 1 to 6; the sheet halves your speed at level 2 and your hit point maximum at level 4, and a long rest takes off one level. Grappled, restrained, and other conditions that stop you moving show your speed as 0.

Inventory, coins, and carrying weight

  • Your starting equipment from the builder is already there. Add gear by name (the box suggests the usual kit and fills in its weight), change how many you have as you use torches and rations, and Unpack a pack such as the explorer's pack into what's inside it.
  • The purse keeps one total. Add or spend coins of any kind (copper, silver, electrum, gold, platinum) and it shows the total in gold, silver, and copper, so nobody has to convert.
  • Carrying capacity is your Strength score × 15 pounds; past it you can only push or drag the load, at 5 feet of speed. Turn on the variant encumbrance rule and you're encumbered past STR × 5 (speed −10 feet) and heavily encumbered past STR × 10 (speed −20 feet, and disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution rolls and on attacks). The speed on the sheet follows along.
  • Pick SRD magic items from the list. Those that need attunement get an Attune button, and you can be attuned to three at once. Each one links to its card with the full description.
  • Wear and Hold switch your armor and shield, and Armor Class changes to match. Weapons you add show up under Attacks.

Works with

Edit the character (or level up) in the Character Builder; the play sheet keeps your current hit points and spent resources and trims them to the new level. Print the features as Feature & Item Cards, work out hit chances with Attack Math, and write the session up in the Player Journal.
